blocks.text: This page tracks the Maple Ridge MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $864,000 for a typical home, down 8.4% over twelve months.
Maple Ridge benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Maple Ridge home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $864,000 in October 2026. That is down 2.1% on the month, down 3.7% over three months, down 6.1% over six months and down 8.4% over the year. Over three years it is down 12.4%, and over five years down 8.8%.
The weakest one-year move in Maple Ridge was for a townhouse homes at −9.5%; the strongest was an apartment at −8.3%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,138,500) and an apartment ($481,600) is $656,900, and a townhouse ($686,600) sits $205,000 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Maple Ridge is 19.1% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 8.4% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Maple Ridge ranks 16 by all-home benchmark, with Burnaby North above it at $875,000 and Port Coquitlam below it at $840,200.

Detached homes in Maple Ridge: benchmark $1,138,500, down 1.5% in a month, down 3.9% in three months, down 7.6% in six months, down 8.6% in a year, down 10.7% in three years and down 7.4% in five. That is 35.9% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Maple Ridge: benchmark $686,600, down 2.0% in a month, down 4.4% in three months, down 5.1% in six months, down 9.5% in a year, down 11.3% in three years and down 3.4% in five. That is 31.8% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Maple Ridge: benchmark $481,600, down 6.2% in a month, down 4.0% in three months, down 4.4% in six months, down 8.3% in a year, down 13.7% in three years and little changed at −0.3% in five. That is 28.5% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Maple Ridge home is worth about $79,200 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $943,200. By type, detached homes lost about $107,100, from $1,245,600 to $1,138,500, townhouses lost about $72,100, from $758,700 to $686,600, and apartments lost about $43,600, from $525,200 to $481,600 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $920,100 six months ago and near $986,300 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $56,100 below the six-month mark and about $122,300 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Maple Ridge benchmark is about $204,600 below the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $184,000 below.
Maple Ridge sales at a glance, past 12 months

Over the past year, 544 Maple Ridge houses sold at a median of $1.18M (middle half $999,975 to $1.35M), half of them within 24 days. 246 condos sold at a median of $463,500 (middle half $390,000 to $532,925), half within 28 days. Quarter by quarter, the median house price eased from $1.18M to $1.16M between November–January and August–October (123 and 118 sales).

blocks.text: What the Maple Ridge figure is
The $864,000 Maple Ridge figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Maple Ridge?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Maple Ridge home was $864,000, with detached at $1,138,500.

faq.q: Are Maple Ridge home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Maple Ridge is down 8.4% over twelve months and down 3.7% over three months.
